package_info.package_versions: Any version uploaded after initial approval (malicious update)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is malicious because it exploits a vulnerability in Jenkins' plugin update process by embedding a cross-site scripting (XSS) payload in the plugin metadata. This allows attacker-controlled JavaScript to execute in the Jenkins admin UI, enabling credential theft or remote code execution when an administrator views the Available Plugin Manager page, even if the plugin is not installed.

execution_context.trigger: When a Jenkins administrator opens the Available Plugin Manager page (metadata fetch and page load)
execution_context.file_location: Plugin HPI file (version attribute) → Update Center JSON → Jenkins admin web UI
required_permissions: Ability to upload plugin updates to Jenkins Update Center
Network access for Update Center sync

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a Jenkins administrator opens the Available Plugin Manager page, the embedded <script> tag in the plugin metadata is rendered and executed by the browser, causing attacker-supplied JavaScript to run in the context of the admin session, which can exfiltrate credentials or perform arbitrary actions on behalf of the admin.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding executable JavaScript within metadata fields, especially in the version attribute, is a direct XSS attack vector. This is highly suspicious in any context, but especially dangerous in privileged admin interfaces.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Plugin metadata fields such as version should only contain plain text values. The presence of HTML or JavaScript in these fields violates the expectation of non-executable, descriptive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason for executable code or HTML tags to appear in plugin version metadata. All such occurrences should be treated as malicious.
key_indicators: Presence of <script> or other HTML tags in plugin metadata fields (e.g., version, description)
JavaScript code embedded in metadata that is rendered in the Jenkins admin UI
Execution of code on page load without user interaction in the plugin manager
Unexpected modification of Update Center JSON to include script tags

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a benign plugin to the Jenkins Update Center to gain initial approval.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains the ability to upload updates to the same plugin.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious update containing an XSS payload in the version attribute of the plugin HPI file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious metadata is stored in the Update Center JSON and distributed to Jenkins servers.

attack_chain.action: Jenkins servers fetch the updated plugin metadata from the Update Center during routine sync.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious payload is now present in local plugin metadata and visible in the admin UI.

attack_chain.action: Jenkins administrator opens the Available Plugin Manager page, causing the XSS payload to execute in the browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker-controlled JavaScript executes in the admin's browser session, enabling credential theft or remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Rendering or execution of <script> or other HTML tags from plugin metadata fields in the Jenkins admin UI
Execution of JavaScript originating from plugin metadata when the Available Plugin Manager page is loaded
Unexpected network requests initiated from the admin UI page to external or untrusted domains during plugin management operations
file_indicators: Update Center JSON files containing <script> tags or HTML in version or description fields
HPI plugin files with metadata fields (e.g., version) containing non-standard content such as HTML or JavaScript
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP or HTTPS requests from Jenkins admin UI to attacker-controlled domains triggered by plugin metadata
Unexpected requests to external domains initiated during admin UI page loads or plugin metadata rendering
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automatically scan plugin metadata in both HPI files and Update Center JSON for embedded <script> tags or suspicious HTML/JavaScript content in fields such as version or description. Monitor the Jenkins admin UI for execution of JavaScript not originating from official Jenkins sources. Set alerts for any network requests initiated from the admin UI to untrusted or external domains, especially during plugin management or metadata rendering operations.
